newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian salt monopoly seen privatised in April.
newsitem.headline: Austrian salt monopoly seen privatised in April.

text.p: The deadline for bids for Austrian government sell-off candidate Salinen AG ends on Friday and the new owner is expected to be announced in April, Austrian radio said.
Austrian state holding company OeIAG took over the business of salt monopoly Salinen from the state last August to prepare it for privatisation.
OeIAG finance chief Erich Becker told state radio that some offers had already landed on his desk but that he had yet to look at them.
"We will analyse the offers, but as this process is very time-consuming the new owner will most likely be announced in April," Becker said.
Although the deadline ends on Friday, offers from other interested parties would still be considered up until the end of next week.
Becker stressed that the salt producer would be sold to the party making the highest bid and with the most viable concept in order to comply with Austrian privatisation laws.

Recent media reports say that more than 10 offers have been made for Salinen, among them sugar and starch producer Agrana Beteiligungs-AG and former finance minister Hannes Androsch, who was reported to have put up some 700 million schillings ($60 million) for the company.
Becker said the OeIAG's next privatisation would be Austria Tabak AG, which would "most likely be floated on the stock exchange." -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 253 ($ = 11.69 Austrian Schillings)
